([[Toronto, Ontario]]) *[[Findlay Prep]]
([[Henderson, Nevada]]) | college = [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] (2014–2017) | draft_year = 2017 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 45 | draft_team = [[Houston Rockets]] | career_start = 2017 | years1 = {{nbay|2017|start}}–{{nbay|2022|end}} | team1 = [[Memphis Grizzlies]] | years2 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team2 = [[Houston Rockets]] | years3 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team3 = [[Phoenix Suns]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] ({{nbay|2022|end}}) * Consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2017 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2017]]) * Third-team All-American – [[Sporting News|SN]] ([[2016 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2016]]) * [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]] ([[2016–17 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|2017]]) * 2× First-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] ([[2015–16 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|2016]], 2017) * [[Pac-12]] All-Freshman team (2015) | medaltemplates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|CAN}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Basketball World Cup|FIBA World Cup]]}} {{MedalBronze|[[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2023 Philippines–Japan–Indonesia]]|}} {{MedalCompetition|[[Pan American Games]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2015 Pan American Games|2015 Toronto]]|[[Basketball at the 2015 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|Team]]}} }} '''Dillon Brooks''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|d|ɪ|l|ən}} {{respell|DIL|ən}};{{cite press release |author= |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 17, 2024}} born January 22, 1996) is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Phoenix Suns]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]], where he was named a consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and earned [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|conference player of the year]] honors in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]] in 2017. Brooks was selected in the second round of the [[2017 NBA draft]]. He began his career with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], earning [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] honors in 2023. He was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in July 2023 and was later dealt to the Suns after two seasons with Houston. In the same year, Brooks was named the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup|Best Defensive Player]] after helping the [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canada national team]] to bronze in the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup|FIBA Basketball World Cup]].{{Cite web | title=How the NBA's biggest villain helped turn around two franchises - ESPN | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47602565/dillon-brooks-phoenix-suns-dillon-villain-nba | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260115123554/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47602565/dillon-brooks-phoenix-suns-dillon-villain-nba | access-date=2026-08-29 | archive-date=2026-01-15}} Brooks has developed a controversial reputation for his trash talk and physical play, though others consider him a culture setter. Embracing the attention surrounding his on-court persona, he has adopted the nickname "'''(Dillon) the Villain'''".{{Cite web |date=2025-12-07 |title=Suns Star Dillon Brooks Channels Inner Kobe With Villain Nickname |url=https://www.si.com/nba/suns/onsi/news/phoenix-suns-star-dillon-brooks-channels-inner-kobe-bryant-villain-nickname |access-date=2026-05-29 |website=Phoenix Suns On SI |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/35769523/dillon-brooks-wants-stay-mad|title=Dillon Brooks wants you to stay mad|author=Tim Keown|date=March 3, 2023 |access-date=2026-05-29 |website=www.espn.com}} ==College career== [[File:Dillon Brooks (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Brooks with [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] in 2015]] Brooks, a [[small forward]] from [[Mississauga]], [[Ontario]], went to the [[University of Oregon]] after playing at [[Father Henry Carr Catholic Secondary School]] in [[Toronto]] and [[Findlay Prep]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]]. As a freshman, he averaged 11.5 points per game and was named to the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12 Conference]] all-freshman team. As a sophomore, Brooks led the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Ducks]] to the [[Pac-12 Conference]] regular season title and a top ten national ranking. At the close of the season, he was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]]{{cite web | last = Alger| first = Tyson| title = Dillon Brooks and Elgin Cook earn 1st-team all-Pac-12 honors | work = [[The Oregonian]] | date = March 7, 2016 | url = http://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/index.ssf/2016/03/dillon_brooks_and_elgin_cook_e.html | access-date = March 12, 2016}} and a third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by the [[Sporting News]]. He was also named the District IX player of the year by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] (USBWA).{{cite web | last = Alger| first = Tyson| title = Dana Altman and Dillon Brooks win U.S. Basketball Writers Association awards | work = [[The Oregonian]] | date = March 8, 2016 | url = http://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/index.ssf/2016/03/dana_altman_and_dillon_brooks.html | access-date = March 12, 2016}} Brooks averaged 16.7 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 3.1 assists per game.{{cite news|last=Medcalf|first=Myron|title=With a healthy Dillon Brooks, Oregon can crash party and win it all|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/116130|access-date=October 11, 2016|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=October 4, 2016}} After the conclusion of the 2015–16 season, Brooks said he would remain with Oregon for a third season.{{cite web|url=http://oregon.247sports.com/Bolt/Dillon-Brooks-Addresses-NBA-Decision--44496207|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330184616/http://oregon.247sports.com/Bolt/Dillon-Brooks-Addresses-NBA-Decision--44496207|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 30, 2016|title=Dillon Brooks Addresses NBA Decision|author=Prehm, Matt|publisher=247 Sports|date=March 26, 2016|access-date=March 27, 2016}} He suffered a foot injury in the summer of 2016 and did not play in Oregon's offseason trip to Spain. On November 7, 2016, Brooks was named to the [[Associated Press]]' preseason All-America team.{{cite news|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/duke-s-allen-leads-ap-preseason-all-america-team-110216 |title=Duke's Allen leads AP preseason All-America team |work=[[Fox Sports]] |date=November 2, 2016 |access-date=November 12, 2016}} During his three seasons of college career Brooks averaged 14.8 points, 4.5 rebounds and 2.6 assists in 28.9 minutes per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/brookdi01.html#all_all_college_stats|title=Dillon Brooks Stats|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=December 4, 2018}} Shortly after the [[2016–17 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|2016–17 season]], he declared himself eligible for the [[2017 NBA draft]] and hired an [[Sports agent|agent]], ending his college career.{{cite news|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/index.ssf/2017/04/dillon_brooks_oregon_career_is.html |title=Dillon Brooks' Oregon career is over as he declares for NBA draft, hires agent |first=Andrew |last=Greif |newspaper=[[The Oregonian]] |date=April 12, 2017 |access-date=May 1, 2017}} ==Professional career== ===Memphis Grizzlies (2017–2023)=== Brooks was drafted by the [[Houston Rockets]] with the 45th pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] and then was immediately traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite news|title=Canadian Dillon Brooks selected 45th overall, traded to Grizzlies|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/canadian-dillon-brooks-selected-45th-overall-grizzlies/|access-date=June 23, 2017|work=Sportsnet|date=June 22, 2017}} On July 21, 2017, the Grizzlies signed Brooks to his rookie scale contract.{{Cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/breaking-grizzlies-sign-oregon-product-dillon-brooks-to-3-year-rookie-deal/|title=Breaking: Grizzlies sign Oregon product Dillon Brooks to 3-year rookie deal|last=Manrique|first=Bruno|date=July 21, 2017|website=clutchpoints.com|access-date=July 22, 2017}} On October 18, 2017, during the Grizzlies' season opener, Brooks scored 19 points, the most points scored by a Canadian-born player in an NBA debut.{{cite web|title=Dillon Brooks sets Canadian record with 19 points in NBA debut|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/dillon-brooks-sets-canadian-record-19-points-nba-debut/|website=Sportsnet.ca|access-date=October 19, 2017}} On April 11, 2018, Brooks scored 36 points along with seven rebounds, one assist, and two steals in a 137–123 loss against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|title=Grizzlies' Dillon Brooks:Scores career-high 36 points in Wednesday's loss|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-dillon-brooks-scores-career-high-36-points-in-wednesdays-loss/|work=CBS Sports|date=April 12, 2018|access-date=March 2, 2020}} In December 2018, Brooks was thought to be involved in a failed three-way trade between Memphis, the [[Washington Wizards]] and the [[Phoenix Suns]]; the trade faltered over confusion between Brooks and his similarly named teammate, [[MarShon Brooks]],{{cite web |last=Wright |first=Michael C. |title=1 year later: The 'awkward' NBA trade that never happened due to last names |url=https://www.nba.com/news/fallout-bizarre-trevor-ariza-dillon-marshon-brooks-trade |publisher=National Basketball Association |access-date=May 24, 2021}} as the Memphis front office did not intend to trade Dillon while the other teams expected him and not MarShon. On January 5, 2019, Brooks suffered from a ruptured ligament in his right big toe{{cite web|title=Dillon Brooks medical update|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/dillon-brooks-medical-update-190109|date=January 9, 2019|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=January 9, 2019}} and underwent a successful surgery to repair it on January 11, 2019. Brooks missed the remainder of the 2018–19 season.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3155526|title=Dillon Brooks Stats, News, Bio|website=ESPN.com}} [[File:Dillion Brooks with picture for his Apartment (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|left|Brooks in 2018]] Brooks began the 2019–20 season as the Grizzlies' starting shooting guard. After averaging 16.1 points per game over the first half of the season, on February 5, 2020, he signed a three-year, $35 million extension with the Grizzlies.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-dillon-brooks-to-multi-year-contract-extension-200205|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Dillon Brooks to multi-year contract extension|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 6, 2020}} On February 28, 2020, Brooks scored a season-high 32 points, along with getting two rebounds, one assist and one block in a 104–101 loss against the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-dillon-brooks-scores-season-high-32-points/|title=Grizzlies' Dillon Brooks: Scores season-high 32 points|date=February 29, 2020|work=CBS Sports|access-date=March 2, 2020}} On May 23, 2021, Brooks made his NBA playoff debut, scoring a season-high 31 points, along with seven rebounds, to help the Grizzlies to a 112–109 Game 1 victory over the top-seeded [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web |last=Polacek |first=Scott |date=May 23, 2021 |title=Ja Morant, Dillon Brooks Lead Grizzlies to Game 1 Upset of Mike Conley, Jazz |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10003550-ja-morant-dillon-brooks-lead-grizzlies-to-game-1-upset-of-mike-conley-jazz |access-date=May 23, 2021 |website=bleacherreport.com}} The Grizzlies would go on to get eliminated and lose the series in five games.{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31557773|title=Utah Jazz use lessons from last postseason's blown 3–1 lead to close out Memphis Grizzlies|publisher=ESPN|access-date=June 3, 2021|date=June 2, 2021}} On October 12, 2021, it was announced that Brooks would miss two to three weeks due to a fracture in his left hand.{{cite news |last=Barnes |first=Evan |title=Grizzlies' Dillon Brooks to miss start of regular season due to left hand injury |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/nba/grizzlies/2021/10/12/dillon-brooks-injury-memphis-grizzlies-miss-start-nba-season/8427248002/ |access-date=October 13, 2021 |work=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |date=October 12, 2021}} On December 19, he scored a career high 37 points in a 105–100 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite news |last=Barnes |first=Evan |title=Grizzlies' Dillon Brooks: Explodes for career-high 37 points|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-dillon-brooks-explodes-for-career-high-37-points/|access-date=December 20, 2021 |work=CBS Sports|date=December 31, 2021}} On January 8, 2022, during a 123–108 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], Brooks suffered a left ankle injury. The next day, he was ruled out for 3-to-5 weeks with injury, which was diagnosed as an ankle sprain.{{Cite web |title=Dillon Brooks injury update: Grizzlies forward to miss at least 3–5 weeks with sprained ankle, per report |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/dillon-brooks-injury-update-grizzlies-forward-to-miss-at-least-3-5-weeks-with-sprained-ankle-per-report/ |access-date=April 16, 2022 |work=CBS Sports|date=January 9, 2022 }} On April 16, during Game 1 of the first round of the playoffs, Brooks scored 24 points in a 117–130 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{Cite web |title=Timberwolves stun Grizzlies, grab Game 1 with 130–117 win |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/timberwolves-stun-grizzlies-grab-game-1-with-130-117-win/ |access-date=April 16, 2022 |work=CBS Sports}} In Game 2 of the 2022 [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]] semifinals against the [[Golden State Warriors]], Brooks was assessed a [[flagrant 2]] and ejected after he chased down the Warriors' [[Gary Payton II]] and hit him in the head when he was in the air, going up for a fast-break layup; Payton fell hard and fractured his left elbow.{{cite news |last=Andrews |first=Kendra |author-link=Kendra Andrews |date=May 4, 2022 |title=Golden State Warriors' Gary Payton II expected to miss about a month with fractured elbow, sources say |publisher=ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33857742 |access-date=May 4, 2022}} Brooks was suspended for Game 3 of the series.{{Cite web |last=Youngmisuk |first=Ohm |date=May 5, 2022 |title=NBA suspends Brooks for Game 3 vs. Warriors |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33861821 |access-date=May 5, 2022 |publisher=ESPN}} The Grizzlies would go on to lose the series in six games. On December 17, 2022, Brooks scored a team-leading 32 points during a 115–109 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468598 Grizzlies star Morant ejected, short-handed Thunder win] On February 2, 2023, Brooks was assessed a flagrant 2 foul and ejected for punching [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] player [[Donovan Mitchell]] in the groin.{{Cite web |last=Crane |first=Andrew |date=February 3, 2023 |title=Dillon Brooks punches Donovan Mitchell, setting off brawl |url=https://nypost.com/2023/02/02/dillon-brooks-punches-donovan-mitchell-setting-off-brawl/ |access-date=February 3, 2023 |work=New York Post}} The next day, the NBA suspended Brooks for one game without pay for his actions.{{Cite web |date=February 3, 2023 |title=Dillon Brooks suspended 1 Basketball Association}} On March 4, he was suspended for one game without pay for incurring his 16th technical foul of the season.{{Cite web |title=Rockets' Dillon Brooks suspended 1 game for receiving 16th technical|url=https://www.nba.com/news/rockets-dillon-brooks-suspended-1-game-for-receiving-16th-technical |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=NBA.com}}{{cite tweet|author=NBA Communications|user=NBAPR|number=1632112512152879105|title=The following was released by the NBA.|date=March 4, 2023|access-date=March 4, 2023}} On March 17, Brooks was fined $35,000 by the NBA after he shoved a cameraman to the floor during a game two days earlier against the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite news |date=March 17, 2023 |title=NBA fines Grizzlies' Brooks $35K for shoving camera person |work=Associated Press News |url=https://apnews.com/article/nba-memphis-grizzlies-dillon-brooks-fined-shoving-cameraman-aa4f1754382285fb697b77f539ab8ab8 |access-date=December 18, 2023}} On March 21, Communications|user=NBAPR|number=1638284498088370179|title=The following was released by the NBA.|date=March 21, 2023|access-date=March 21, 2023}}{{Cite web |date=2023-03-21 |title=Brooks' taunts draw 18th tech, auto 1-game ban |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/35908692/dillon-brooks-faces-1-game-suspension-taunting-mavs-bench |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=ESPN.com}} At the end of the season, Brooks was named for the first time to the [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive Second team]].{{Cite web |title=Jaren Jackson Jr. headlines 2022–23 Kia NBA All-Defensive teams |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2022-23-all-defensive-teams-announced |access-date=May 9, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} During Memphis' [[2023 NBA playoffs]] series against the magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2023/04/21/lebron-james-trash-talk-poke-the-bear-dillon-brooks-nba-playoffs|title=Hey, Dillon Brooks, Poke LeBron James at Your Own threes|work=ClutchPoints|last=Donabedian|first=Daniel|date=January 27, 2025|access-date=January 27, 2025}} ===Phoenix Suns (2025–present)=== On July 6, 2025, Brooks, alongside [[Jalen Green]], was |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/phoenix-suns-acquire-dillon-brooks-jalen-green-and-draft-rights-to-khaman-maluach-rasheer-fleming-and-koby-brea-in-seven-team-trade |access-date=July 6, 2025 after receiving his 18th [[technical foul]] in the game against the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web |title=Dillon Brooks avoids suspension after NBA review |url=https://basketnews.com/news-244532-dillon-brooks-avoids-suspension-after-nba-review.html#google_vignette |website=basketnews.com |access-date=15 April 2026 |language=en}} During the season, Brooks averaged a career-high 20.2 points per game and helped the Suns finish with a 45–37 record, exceeding expectations after a disappointing 2024–25 season.{{Cite web |title=The Phoenix Suns' season just ended — but it largely defied expectations |url=https://www.kjzz.org/the-show/2026-05-01/the-phoenix-suns-season-just-ended-but-it-largely-defied-expectations |access-date=May 1, 2026 |website=KJZZ}} Going into the playoffs, the eighth-seeded Suns faced the reigning champion and top seed [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] during their first-round series. Brooks made his playoff debut for the Suns on April 19, recording 18 points, seven rebounds, and two assists in a 119–84 Game 1 loss.{{Cite web |title=GILGEOUS-ALEXANDER SCORES 25 AS REIGNING CHAMPION THUNDER OPEN PLAYOFFS WITH 119-84 WIN OVER SUNS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042500141 |access-date=May 1, 2026 |website=NBA.com}} On April 22, he put up 30 points and six rebounds in a 120–107 Game 2 loss.{{Cite web |title=GILGEOUS-ALEXANDER SCORES 37 AS THE THUNDER BEAT THE SUNS TO GO UP 2-0 IN THEIR 1ST-ROUND SERIES |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042500142 |access-date=May 1, 2026 |website=NBA.com}} On April 25, Brooks scored a playoff career-high 33 points, alongside seven rebounds, in a 121–109 Game 3 loss.{{Cite web |title=GILGEOUS-ALEXANDER SCORES 42, THUNDER BEAT SUNS 121-109 TO TAKE A 3-0 SERIES LEAD |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042500143 |access-date=May 1, 2026 |website=NBA.com}} The Suns wound up being swept by the Thunder, with Brooks averaging 26.0 points per game as their leading scorer in the playoffs. On August 5, [[List of 2026–27 NBA season transactions|2026]], the Suns and Brooks agreed to a three–year, $73 million contract extension, locking him in through the 2029–30 season.{{cite news |last1=Charania |first1=Shams |last2=Wright |first2=Michael |title=Suns keeping Dillon Brooks on $73M extension through 2029-30 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49541747/suns-keeping-dillon-brooks-73m-extension-2029-30 |access-date=5 August 2026 |date=5 August 2026}}{{cite news |last1=Villas |first1=Rexwell |title=Dillon Brooks lands $73 million contract extension with Suns |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/dillon-brooks-lands-73-million-013529815.html |access-date=5 August 2026 |date=August 5, 2026}} ==National team career== [[File:2023-08-09 Deutschland gegen Kanada (Basketball-Länderspiel) by Sandro Halank–094.jpg|thumb|upright|Brooks with Canada prior to the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]]]] Brooks played for the [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canadian national team]] in the [[Basketball at the 2015 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|2015 Pan American Games]], where the team won the silver medal.{{cite web|last=Denomme|first=Ian|title=Canada settles for silver in basketball at Pan Am Games, but future looks bright | publisher=[[Yahoo!]]|date=July 25, 2016|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/blogs/eh-game/canada-settles-for-silver-in-basketball-at-pan-am-games--but-future-looks-bright-000909709.html|access-date=March 12, 2016}} On May 24, 2022, Brooks was one of fourteen players to agree to a three-year commitment to play with the Canadian senior men's national team, aiming to break a decades-long trend of failing to qualify for the [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|Olympic basketball tournament]].{{Cite web |title=Fourteen Athletes Committed to Represent Canada As Senior Men's National Team Summer Core Revealed |url=https://www.basketball.ca/news/athletes-committed-to-represent-canada-as-senior-mens-national-team-summer-core-revealed |access-date=May 24, 2022 |work=Canada Basketball}} They achieved this goal at the [[2023 FIBA World Cup]], and won the bronze medal, Canada's first global tournament medal in basketball since [[Basketball at the 1936 Summer Olympics|1936]]. Brooks played a crucial role, recording a team-best 39 points in their victory over the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]].{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/olympics/summer/basketball/world-cup-basketball-men-canada-united-states-bronze-recap-1.6962177|title=Canada holds off U.S. to win bronze at men's Basketball World Cup in OT|website=[[CBC Sports]]|last=Reynolds|first=Tim|access-date=September 10, 2023 |date=September 10, 2023}} This was a single-game scoring record for a Canadian player at the World Cup, surpassing [[Carl Ridd]]'s previous high of 37 at the [[1954 FIBA World Championship|1954 edition]].{{cite news|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/basketball/article-canada-defeats-us-in-overtime-to-claim-bronze-first-ever-medal-at-fiba/|title=Canada defeats U.S. in overtime to claim bronze, first-ever medal at FIBA World Cup|newspaper=[[The Globe & Mail]]|access-date=September 10, 2023 |date=September 10, 2023}} Brooks was named Best Defensive Player of the tournament by [[FIBA]].{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/news/world-cup-2023-all-second-team-best-coach-and-best-defensive-player-awards-revealed|title=World Cup 2023 All-Second Team, Best Coach and Best Defensive Player Awards revealed|publisher=[[FIBA]]|date=September 10, 2023|access-date=September 10, 2023}} He was named to Canada's roster for the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Summer Olympics in Paris]].{{cite web| title = Gilgeous-Alexander, Murray to lead NBA-experienced Canadian Olympic team in Paris| publisher = CBC / The Canadian Press | url = https://www.cbc.ca/sports/olympics/summer/basketball/canada-olympic-mens-basketball-roster-paris-1.7259301 | access-date = July 10, 2014}} After a strong unbeaten performance in the group stage, which was deemed the "group of death" by experts,{{cite web |title=Fans celebrate after Canada sweeps 'Group of Death' |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/olympics/article/fans-celebrate-after-canada-sweeps-group-of-death/ |website=Sportsnet |publisher=Sportsnet |access-date=April 17, 2026}} Canada was surprisingly eliminated in the quarterfinals by hosts [[France|France.]]{{cite web |title=Doing it the French way: Hosts eliminate unbeaten Canada |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/news/doing-it-the-french-way-hosts-eliminate-previously-unbeaten-canada |website=FIBA Basketball |publisher=FIBA |access-date=18 April 2026}}. Brooks averaged 11.3 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 1.5 assists over 4 games.{{cite web |title=2024 Team Canada Olympic Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/teams/canada/2024.html |website=Basketball Reference |publisher=Basketball Reference |access-date=18 April 2026}} == Business ventures == In 2024, Brooks became an angel investor in Panda Hub, a mobile car detailing marketplace operating in North America. His involvement began as a customer in Houston, Texas, where he utilized the service and later decided to invest, citing the company's innovative approach to simplifying car care through technology.{{cite web |date=April 11, 2024 |title=NBA player Dillon Brooks on how he invests the $125 million he's made — and which opponent is the hardest to defend |url=https://www.marketwatch.com/story/nba-player-dillon-brooks-on-how-he-invests-the-125-million-hes-made-and-which-opponent-is-the-hardest-to-defend-1866f165 |access-date=June 4, 2025 |work=MarketWatch}}{{cite web |date=March 29, 2024 |title=Panda Hub Proudly Announces Partnership With Dillon Brooks And Expansion To Houston, Texas |url=https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/203606/Panda-Hub-Proudly-Announces-Partnership-With-Dillon-Brooks-And-Expansion-To-Houston-Texas |access-date=June 4, 2025 |website=Newsfile}}{{cite web |date=May 14, 2024 |title=The Business Taking The Car Detailing Industry By Storm, Investors, Expansion And More |url=https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/the-business-taking-the-car-detailing-industry-by-storm-investors-expansion-and-more-833486310.html |access-date=June 4, 2025 |website=Newswire}}{{Cite web |title=Success Story: Dillon Brooks Angel Investor {{!}} Panda Hub |url=https://www.pandahub.com/dillon-brooks |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=www.pandahub.com}} ==Personal life== On June 26, 2025, [[TMZ]] first reported that Brooks was filing a restraining order on his now ex-girlfriend Heather Andrews (who first met Brooks back in 2018 and later birthed two children with him while they were together) due to her destroying his belongings and enacting other dangerous behavior against him that would have hurt him personally and/or professionally, including threats of cutting off all of his fingers and even threatening Brooks' own mom.{{cite web |author1=T.M.Z. Staff |title=NBA's Dillon Brooks Files For Restraining Order Against Ex |url=https://www.tmz.com/2025/06/26/dillon-brooks-files-for-restraining-order-against-ex/ |website=TMZ |publisher=EHM Productions Inc. |access-date=6 November 2025 |language=en |date=26 June 2025}} His restraining order would come one year after Andrews submitted her own restraining order against him. On March 6, 2026, Brooks was reportedly arrested for [[driving under the influence]] in [[Scottsdale, Arizona]].{{cite web |title=Dillon Brooks arrested for driving under the influence |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1940113/dillon-brooks-arrested-for-driving-under-the-influence/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=6 March 2026 |language=en |date=6 March 2026}} ==Career
